solution:
The constraints are \(x \le 4\), \(y \le 6\), \(x + y \le 6\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

The boundary lines are \(x = 4\), \(y = 6\) and \(x + y = 6\). The relevant corner points of the feasible region are:

\(x = 4\) meets \(x + y = 6\): put \(x = 4\) in \(x + y = 6\) to get \(y = 2\), giving \((4, 2)\).
\(x + y = 6\) meets \(x = 0\) at \((0, 6)\) (which also lies on \(y = 6\)).

So the corner points are \(O(0,0)\), \((4,0)\), \((4,2)\) and \((0,6)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 11x + 8y\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((4,0)\) | \(44\) |
| \((4,2)\) | \(60\) |
| \((0,6)\) | \(48\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(60\), attained at \((x, y) = (4, 2)\).

The constraints are \(3x + 2y \le 12\), \(x + y \ge 4\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(3x + 2y = 12\) meets the axes at \((4,0)\) and \((0,6)\); \(x + y = 4\) meets the axes at \((4,0)\) and \((0,4)\).

Intersection of the two lines: from \(x + y = 4\), \(x = 4 - y\). Substitute in \(3x + 2y = 12\): \(3(4 - y) + 2y = 12 \Rightarrow 12 - y = 12 \Rightarrow y = 0,\ x = 4\). They meet at \((4, 0)\).

The feasible region (above \(x + y = 4\), below \(3x + 2y = 12\)) is the triangle with corner points \((4,0)\), \((0,4)\) and \((0,6)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 4x + 6y\) |
|---|---|
| \((4,0)\) | \(16\) |
| \((0,4)\) | \(24\) |
| \((0,6)\) | \(36\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(36\), attained at \((x, y) = (0, 6)\).

The constraints are \(3x + 5y \le 26\), \(5x + 3y \le 30\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(3x + 5y = 26\) meets the axes at \((\tfrac{26}{3}, 0)\) and \((0, 5.2)\); \(5x + 3y = 30\) meets the axes at \((6, 0)\) and \((0, 10)\).

On the \(x\)-axis the binding point is \((6, 0)\) (from \(5x + 3y = 30\); it satisfies \(3x + 5y = 18 \le 26\)). On the \(y\)-axis the binding point is \((0, 5.2)\) (from \(3x + 5y = 26\); it satisfies \(5x + 3y = 15.6 \le 30\)).

Intersection of the two lines:
\(3x + 5y = 26\) ... (i), \(5x + 3y = 30\) ... (ii).
\((i)\times 3:\ 9x + 15y = 78\); \((ii)\times 5:\ 25x + 15y = 150\). Subtracting, \(16x = 72 \Rightarrow x = 4.5\). Then \(3(4.5) + 5y = 26 \Rightarrow 5y = 12.5 \Rightarrow y = 2.5\). So they meet at \((4.5, 2.5)\).

Corner points: \(O(0,0)\), \((6,0)\), \((4.5, 2.5)\), \((0, 5.2)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 7x + 11y\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((6,0)\) | \(42\) |
| \((4.5, 2.5)\) | \(59\) |
| \((0, 5.2)\) | \(57.2\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(59\), attained at \((x, y) = (4.5, 2.5)\).

The constraints are \(x + 4y \le 24\), \(3x + y \le 21\), \(x + y \le 9\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(x + 4y = 24\) meets axes at \((24,0)\), \((0,6)\); \(3x + y = 21\) at \((7,0)\), \((0,21)\); \(x + y = 9\) at \((9,0)\), \((0,9)\).

On the \(x\)-axis the binding point is \((7, 0)\) (from \(3x + y = 21\)). On the \(y\)-axis the binding point is \((0, 6)\) (from \(x + 4y = 24\)).

Intersection of \(3x + y = 21\) and \(x + y = 9\): subtracting, \(2x = 12 \Rightarrow x = 6,\ y = 3\), giving \((6, 3)\) (it satisfies \(x + 4y = 18 \le 24\)).
Intersection of \(x + y = 9\) and \(x + 4y = 24\): subtracting, \(3y = 15 \Rightarrow y = 5,\ x = 4\), giving \((4, 5)\) (it satisfies \(3x + y = 17 \le 21\)).

Corner points: \(O(0,0)\), \((7,0)\), \((6,3)\), \((4,5)\), \((0,6)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 3x + 5y\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((7,0)\) | \(21\) |
| \((6,3)\) | \(33\) |
| \((4,5)\) | \(37\) |
| \((0,6)\) | \(30\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(37\), attained at \((x, y) = (4, 5)\).

The constraints are \(5x + y \ge 5\), \(x + y \ge 3\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(5x + y = 5\) meets axes at \((1,0)\), \((0,5)\); \(x + y = 3\) meets axes at \((3,0)\), \((0,3)\).

The feasible region lies above both lines (unbounded above). Its corner points:

On the \(y\)-axis the binding point is \((0, 5)\) (from \(5x + y = 5\); it satisfies \(x + y = 5 \ge 3\)).
On the \(x\)-axis the binding point is \((3, 0)\) (from \(x + y = 3\); it satisfies \(5x + y = 15 \ge 5\)).
Intersection of \(5x + y = 5\) and \(x + y = 3\): subtracting, \(4x = 2 \Rightarrow x = 0.5,\ y = 2.5\), giving \((0.5, 2.5)\).

Corner points: \((0,5)\), \((0.5, 2.5)\), \((3,0)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 7x + y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,5)\) | \(5\) |
| \((0.5, 2.5)\) | \(6\) |
| \((3,0)\) | \(21\) |

The region is unbounded, but since we minimize, the minimum exists. The minimum value of \(z\) is \(5\), attained at \((x, y) = (0, 5)\).

solution:
The constraints are \(2x + y \ge 7\), \(2x + 3y \ge 15\), \(y \ge 2\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(2x + y = 7\) meets axes at \((3.5,0)\), \((0,7)\); \(2x + 3y = 15\) at \((7.5,0)\), \((0,5)\); and \(y = 2\).

The feasible region lies above all three lines (unbounded above). Its corner points:

On the \(y\)-axis: \(2x + y \ge 7\) needs \(y \ge 7\) at \(x = 0\), giving \((0, 7)\) (it satisfies \(2x + 3y = 21 \ge 15\)).
Intersection of \(2x + y = 7\) and \(2x + 3y = 15\): subtracting, \(2y = 8 \Rightarrow y = 4\), then \(2x = 7 - 4 = 3 \Rightarrow x = 1.5\), giving \((1.5, 4)\) (\(y = 4 \ge 2\)).
Intersection of \(2x + 3y = 15\) and \(y = 2\): \(2x + 6 = 15 \Rightarrow x = 4.5\), giving \((4.5, 2)\) (it satisfies \(2x + y = 11 \ge 7\)).

Corner points: \((0,7)\), \((1.5, 4)\), \((4.5, 2)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 8x + 10y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,7)\) | \(70\) |
| \((1.5, 4)\) | \(52\) |
| \((4.5, 2)\) | \(56\) |

The region is unbounded, but since we minimize, the minimum exists. The minimum value of \(z\) is \(52\), attained at \((x, y) = (1.5, 4)\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives "minimum 22.5 at \((2, 0.5)\)" — that is the minimum of \(z = 6x + 21y\); for the printed objective \(z = 6x + 2y\) the minimum is \(6\), attained along the segment \((0, 3)\)–\((0.6, 1.2)\) (our answer).]

The constraints are \(x + 2y \ge 3\), \(x + 4y \ge 4\), \(3x + y \ge 3\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(x + 2y = 3\) meets axes at \((3,0)\), \((0,1.5)\); \(x + 4y = 4\) at \((4,0)\), \((0,1)\); \(3x + y = 3\) at \((1,0)\), \((0,3)\).

The feasible region lies above all three lines (unbounded above). Its corner points:

On the \(y\)-axis: \(3x + y \ge 3\) needs \(y \ge 3\) at \(x = 0\), giving \((0, 3)\) (satisfies the other two).
Intersection of \(3x + y = 3\) and \(x + 2y = 3\): from \(y = 3 - 3x\), \(x + 2(3 - 3x) = 3 \Rightarrow -5x = -3 \Rightarrow x = 0.6,\ y = 1.2\), giving \((0.6, 1.2)\) (satisfies \(x + 4y = 5.4 \ge 4\)).
Intersection of \(x + 2y = 3\) and \(x + 4y = 4\): subtracting, \(2y = 1 \Rightarrow y = 0.5,\ x = 2\), giving \((2, 0.5)\) (satisfies \(3x + y = 6.5 \ge 3\)).
On the \(x\)-axis: \(x + 4y \ge 4\) needs \(x \ge 4\), giving \((4, 0)\).

Corner points: \((0,3)\), \((0.6, 1.2)\), \((2, 0.5)\), \((4, 0)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 6x + 2y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,3)\) | \(6\) |
| \((0.6, 1.2)\) | \(6\) |
| \((2, 0.5)\) | \(13\) |
| \((4, 0)\) | \(24\) |

The minimum value of \(z\) is \(6\). It occurs at two corner points \((0, 3)\) and \((0.6, 1.2)\), hence at every point on the segment joining them (multiple optimal solutions). The minimum value of \(z\) is \(6\).

[Textbook note: the question says "Maximize \(z = 4x + 2y\)", but over this all-\(\ge\) region \(z\) is unbounded (no maximum); the answer key's "\(\min z = 48\) at \((3, 18)\)" answers the Minimize version.]

The constraints are \(3x + y \ge 27\), \(x + y \ge 21\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(3x + y = 27\) meets axes at \((9,0)\), \((0,27)\); \(x + y = 21\) at \((21,0)\), \((0,21)\).

The feasible region lies above both lines and is UNBOUNDED (it extends without limit towards larger \(x\) and \(y\)). Its corner points are:

On the \(y\)-axis: \(3x + y \ge 27\) needs \(y \ge 27\), giving \((0, 27)\) (satisfies \(x + y = 27 \ge 21\)).
Intersection of \(3x + y = 27\) and \(x + y = 21\): subtracting, \(2x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 3,\ y = 18\), giving \((3, 18)\).
On the \(x\)-axis: \(x + y \ge 21\) needs \(x \ge 21\), giving \((21, 0)\) (satisfies \(3x + y = 63 \ge 27\)).

| Corner point | \(z = 4x + 2y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0, 27)\) | \(54\) |
| \((3, 18)\) | \(48\) |
| \((21, 0)\) | \(84\) |

Because the region is unbounded and \(z = 4x + 2y\) increases without limit as \(x, y\) grow (e.g. move along \(x + y = 21\) beyond \((21,0)\) or take large \(x, y\) satisfying both constraints), \(z\) has NO maximum value. Hence this L.P.P. has an **unbounded solution** (no finite maximum).

solution:
The constraints are \(3x + 5y \le 10\), \(5x + 3y \le 15\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(3x + 5y = 10\) meets axes at \((\tfrac{10}{3}, 0)\), \((0, 2)\); \(5x + 3y = 15\) at \((3, 0)\), \((0, 5)\).

On the \(x\)-axis the binding point is \((3, 0)\) (from \(5x + 3y = 15\); satisfies \(3x + 5y = 9 \le 10\)). On the \(y\)-axis the binding point is \((0, 2)\) (from \(3x + 5y = 10\); satisfies \(5x + 3y = 6 \le 15\)).

Intersection of the two lines:
\(3x + 5y = 10\) ... (i), \(5x + 3y = 15\) ... (ii).
\((i)\times 3:\ 9x + 15y = 30\); \((ii)\times 5:\ 25x + 15y = 75\). Subtracting, \(16x = 45 \Rightarrow x = \tfrac{45}{16} = 2.8125\). Then \(y = \dfrac{10 - 3x}{5} = \dfrac{10 - 8.4375}{5} = \tfrac{5}{16} = 0.3125\). So they meet at \(\left(\tfrac{45}{16}, \tfrac{5}{16}\right)\).

Corner points: \(O(0,0)\), \((3,0)\), \(\left(\tfrac{45}{16}, \tfrac{5}{16}\right)\), \((0,2)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 6x + 10y\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((3,0)\) | \(18\) |
| \(\left(\tfrac{45}{16}, \tfrac{5}{16}\right)\) | \(20\) |
| \((0,2)\) | \(20\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(20\). It occurs at two corner points \((0, 2)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{45}{16}, \tfrac{5}{16}\right)\), hence at every point on the segment joining them (multiple optimal solutions). The maximum value of \(z\) is \(20\).

The constraints are \(x - y \ge 3\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary line: \(x - y = 3\) meets the axes at \((3, 0)\) and \((0, -3)\); only the part in the first quadrant is relevant.

The feasible region is \(\{(x, y) : x \ge y + 3,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\}\). This region is UNBOUNDED — for any \(y \ge 0\) we may take \(x\) as large as we like (with \(x \ge y + 3\)). The only corner point is \((3, 0)\) (where \(x - y = 3\) meets \(y = 0\)).

| Corner point | \(z = 2x + 3y\) |
|---|---|
| \((3, 0)\) | \(6\) |

Since the region is unbounded and \(z = 2x + 3y\) increases without limit as \(x\) (and \(y\)) grow within the region, \(z\) has NO maximum value. Hence this L.P.P. has an **unbounded solution** (no finite maximum).

solution:
Let the variables be \(x_1, x_2\) (plotted as \(x, y\)). The constraints are \(3x_1 + x_2 \le 15\), \(3x_1 + 4x_2 \le 24\), \(x_1 \ge 0\), \(x_2 \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(3x_1 + x_2 = 15\) meets axes at \((5,0)\), \((0,15)\); \(3x_1 + 4x_2 = 24\) at \((8,0)\), \((0,6)\).

On the \(x_1\)-axis the binding point is \((5, 0)\) (from \(3x_1 + x_2 = 15\); satisfies \(3x_1 + 4x_2 = 15 \le 24\)). On the \(x_2\)-axis the binding point is \((0, 6)\) (from \(3x_1 + 4x_2 = 24\); satisfies \(3x_1 + x_2 = 6 \le 15\)).

Intersection of the two lines: subtract \((3x_1 + x_2 = 15)\) from \((3x_1 + 4x_2 = 24)\) to get \(3x_2 = 9 \Rightarrow x_2 = 3\), then \(3x_1 = 15 - 3 = 12 \Rightarrow x_1 = 4\), giving \((4, 3)\).

Corner points: \(O(0,0)\), \((5,0)\), \((4, 3)\), \((0,6)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 4x_1 + 3x_2\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((5,0)\) | \(20\) |
| \((4, 3)\) | \(25\) |
| \((0,6)\) | \(18\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(25\), attained at \((x_1, x_2) = (4, 3)\).

The constraints are \(x + 2y \le 40\), \(3x + 2y \le 60\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(x + 2y = 40\) meets axes at \((40,0)\), \((0,20)\); \(3x + 2y = 60\) at \((20,0)\), \((0,30)\).

On the \(x\)-axis the binding point is \((20, 0)\) (from \(3x + 2y = 60\); satisfies \(x + 2y = 20 \le 40\)). On the \(y\)-axis the binding point is \((0, 20)\) (from \(x + 2y = 40\); satisfies \(3x + 2y = 40 \le 60\)).

Intersection of the two lines: subtract \((x + 2y = 40)\) from \((3x + 2y = 60)\) to get \(2x = 20 \Rightarrow x = 10\), then \(2y = 40 - 10 = 30 \Rightarrow y = 15\), giving \((10, 15)\).

Corner points: \(O(0,0)\), \((20,0)\), \((10, 15)\), \((0,20)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 60x + 50y\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((20,0)\) | \(1200\) |
| \((10, 15)\) | \(1350\) |
| \((0,20)\) | \(1000\) |

The maximum value of \(z\) is \(1350\), attained at \((x, y) = (10, 15)\).

The constraints are \(3x + y \ge 27\), \(x + y \ge 21\), \(x + 2y \ge 30\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Boundary lines: \(3x + y = 27\) meets axes at \((9,0)\), \((0,27)\); \(x + y = 21\) at \((21,0)\), \((0,21)\); \(x + 2y = 30\) at \((30,0)\), \((0,15)\).

The feasible region lies above all three lines and is UNBOUNDED. Its corner points:

On the \(y\)-axis: \(3x + y \ge 27\) needs \(y \ge 27\), giving \((0, 27)\) (satisfies the other two).
Intersection of \(3x + y = 27\) and \(x + y = 21\): subtracting, \(2x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 3,\ y = 18\), giving \((3, 18)\) (satisfies \(x + 2y = 39 \ge 30\)).
Intersection of \(x + y = 21\) and \(x + 2y = 30\): subtracting, \(y = 9,\ x = 12\), giving \((12, 9)\) (satisfies \(3x + y = 45 \ge 27\)).
On the \(x\)-axis: \(x + 2y \ge 30\) needs \(x \ge 30\), giving \((30, 0)\).

| Corner point | \(z = 4x + 2y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0, 27)\) | \(54\) |
| \((3, 18)\) | \(48\) |
| \((12, 9)\) | \(66\) |
| \((30, 0)\) | \(120\) |

Because the region is unbounded and \(z = 4x + 2y\) increases without limit as \(x, y\) grow within the region, \(z\) has NO maximum value. Hence this L.P.P. has an **unbounded solution** (no finite maximum).
